query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a thin layer of Al2O3 via atomic layer deposition (ALD) can improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
generation.intervention: Addition of a thin layer of Al2O3 via ALD
generation.conditions: Temperature: 800°C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 5 hours, Loading: No loading
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a thin layer of Al2O3 on the surface of HfNbTaTiZr
generation.mechanism: The Al2O3 layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, preventing the formation of oxide scales and reducing the oxidation rate of HfNbTaTiZr. This is derived from materials-science principles, as Al2O3 is known to be a stable and impermeable oxide that can protect underlying metals from oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance, with a reduction in oxidation rate and an increase in the time to reach a given level of oxidation.
generation.boundary: Temperature: 800°C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 5 hours, Loading: No loading
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the Al2O3 layer in improving oxygen resistance may depend on the specific processing conditions and the microstructure of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: Expose untreated and Al2O3-coated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr samples to air at 800°C for 5 hours, and measure the oxidation rate and oxide scale thickness.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidation rate and oxide scale thickness of the Al2O3-coated sample are not significantly lower than those of the untreated sample, the hypothesis is falsified.

Abstract: AbstractNowadays refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are regarded as great candidates for the replacement of superalloys at high temperature. To design a RHEA, one must understand the pros and cons of every refractory element. However, the elemental effect on mechanical properties remains unclear. In this study, the subtraction method was applied on equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloys to discover the role of each element, and, thus, HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi were fabricated and analyzed. The microstructure and mechanical properties of each alloy at the as-cast state were examined. The solid solution phase formation rule and the solution strengthening effect are also discussed.
